Created attachment 2732
Convert usages of sprintf in messages/warnings/errors to use gettextf [and similar]

I found some untranslated messages in utils/R/tar.R, e.g.:

https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/efb01627061d5d3ef39c5ff4be0679a59c9439d4/src/library/utils/R/tar.R#L72

```
stop(sprintf("No %s command found", sQuote("gzip")))
```

We can make sure this is translated by using `gettextf()` instead of `sprintf()`.

I wrote a script to detect similar usages in src/library/*/R/*.R and found a slew others.

The attached patch makes the switch wherever I found it.

I suspect some of them were intentionally excluded from translation, but I included a correction in this patch anyway -- my thinking being, any message we're willing to produce in English, we should be willing to attempt to produce in the user's session language.

Here is the script I used for reproducibility:

```
library(lintr)
library(xml2)

setwd('~/svn/R-devel/src/library')

for (f in list.files(pattern = '\\.R$', recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)) {
  src = get_source_expressions(f)
  xml = tail(src[[1L]], 1L)[[1L]]$xml_parsed_content
  
  msg_calls = c("stop", "message", "warning")
  cat_calls = c("sprintf", "paste", "paste0")
  
  expr_cond_fmt = paste(
    "expr[SYMBOL_FUNCTION_CALL[%s]]",
    "expr[expr[SYMBOL_FUNCTION_CALL[%s]]]",
    "not(//SYMBOL_FUNCTION_CALL[text() = 'ngettext'])",
    sep = " and "
  )
  xpath = sprintf(
    '//expr[%s]',
    sprintf(
      expr_cond_fmt,
      paste0("text() = ", dQuote(msg_calls, '"'), collapse = " or "),
      paste0("text() = ", dQuote(cat_calls, '"'), collapse = " or ")
    )
  )
  
  bad_usage = xml_find_all(xml, xpath)
  if (length(bad_usage)) {
    cat("\n\nFound bad usage in ", f, "\n", sep="")
    starts = as.integer(xml_attr(bad_usage, 'line1'))
    ends = as.integer(xml_attr(bad_usage, 'line2'))
    lines = unlist(lapply(seq_along(starts), function(i) seq(starts[i], ends[i])))
    cat(paste0(f, ':', lines, ':', src$lines[lines]), sep = "\n")
  }
}
```

(In reply to Michael Chirico from comment #0)
> Created attachment 2732
.... 
> The attached patch makes the switch wherever I found it.

but it also contains quite a few "white space only" changes (trailing white space)
which are typically frowned on, and you should avoid next time.

More important and general:
Yes, in *some* (relatively rare) cases, I think some of us have intentionally not called `gettext()`  "et al", because the code is "very deep down" in internal evaluation, error handling, etc,  and it may be beneficial when no translation overhead happens at this error signalling state --- and note that "thanks" to  `options(warn = 2)` every warning can also be an error.

We will keep this in mind when looking at your patch
(and I don't promise anything at the moment, but plan to get there within the upcoming 6 days).

noted about the whitespace, sorry about that. my editor auto-trims so I don't even know it happened until I submit.

is there any interest in one big patch to eliminate trailing whitespace? it's pretty inconvenient to have to be wary of this when submitting patches.

comments.text:
Created attachment 3247
Pass untranslated messages through gettext()/gettextf(); use domain=NA consistently on translated messages

Took another pass at this. Whitespace-change-free patch updated. One important change is that I explicitly exclude places where `domain = NA` is passed, which is the proper way to signal "don't translate this".

If some of these messages are not meant to be translated, then we should instead use `domain = NA`.

```
library(lintr) # dev version >= 2a94dab69f3f601d32258a90f4a5e06db4160d74

# this excludes cases where domain=NA is set explicitly
xpath <- "
//SYMBOL_FUNCTION_CALL[text() = 'stop' or text() = 'warning' or text() = 'message']
  /parent::expr[not(OP-DOLLAR)]
  /following-sibling::expr[expr/SYMBOL_FUNCTION_CALL[text() = 'sprintf' or text() = 'paste' or text() = 'paste0']]
  /parent::expr[not(SYMBOL_SUB[text() = 'domain']/following-sibling::*[2]/NUM_CONST[text() = 'NA'])]
"

untranslated_message_linter <- make_linter_from_xpath(xpath, "Untranslated message")

lints <- lint_dir("~/svn/r-devel/src/library", untranslated_message_linter())

subset(
  as.data.frame(lints),
  type != "error" & grepl("/R/", filename),
  c("filename", "line_number", "line")
)
```

As a second pass, I searched for calls to `stop()`/`warning()`/`message()` that call `gettext()`/`gettextf()`/`ngettext()` but don't say `domain=NA`, hinting they'll wastefully attempt translation after it's already been done:

```
xpath <- "
//SYMBOL_FUNCTION_CALL[text() = 'stop' or text() = 'warning' or text() = 'message']
  /parent::expr[not(OP-DOLLAR)]
  /following-sibling::expr[expr/SYMBOL_FUNCTION_CALL[text() = 'gettextf' or text() = 'gettext' or text() = 'ngettext']]
  /parent::expr[not(SYMBOL_SUB[text() = 'domain']/following-sibling::*[2]/NUM_CONST[text() = 'NA'])]
"

retranslated_message_linter <- make_linter_from_xpath(xpath, "Untranslated message")

lints <- lint_dir("~/svn/r-devel/src/library", retranslated_message_linter())

subset(
  as.data.frame(lints),
  type != "error" & grepl("/R/", filename),
  c("filename", "line_number", "line")
)
```

Manuals in package', sQuote(pkg),'

'), makeVignetteTable(cbind(Package=pkg, vinfo[,c("File", "Title", "PDF", "R"), drop = FALSE]))) } ``` Where the HTML header is hard-coded, a well as the string "Manuals in package". Lines 461-468 construct the disambiguation text for when a help topic is found on multiple packages, and "(in package" and "in library" are not translated. On the other hand, line 137 does tag some of the HTML output as translatable with gettext (and some not): ```r .HTMLdirListing <- function(dir, base, up) { files <- list.files(dir) # note, no hidden files are listed out <- HTMLheader(paste0("Listing of directory

", paste0("
", mono(iconv(urls, "", "UTF-8")), "
"), "
") } out <- c(out, "
\n") list(payload = paste(out, collapse="\n")) } ``` Should all these user-facing strings be marked for translation?
